Author: Ajay Bhanot
Bench: Ajay Bhanot
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:27028
Court No. - 64
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 42234 of 2023
Applicant :- Rishiraj Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Akash Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Jitendra Kumar,Keshav Hari Dixit,Purushottam Dixit Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
547 of 2020 at Police Station- Kotwali, District- Etawah, under Sections 498A, 304B, 302/34 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act.
The applicant is in jail since 10.10.2020.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 22.07.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Akash Mishra, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Purushottam Dixit, learned counsel assisted by Shri Jitendra Kumar, learned counsel on behalf of the informant and Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:

sentences.text: 1. The incident occurred at about 12 AM on 07.10.2020.
The police rushed to the site 10 minutes after the deceased were done to death.
2. The FIR was got registered on 08.10.2020 at about 5.16 PM.
3. Delay in lodgement of the FIR in the facts of this case is fatal to the prosecution case.
4. The applicant and his wife(one of the deceased) were estranged.
They were living separately.
5. As per the prosecution case set out in the FIR, the applicant along with five members of his family who were armed to teeth, reached the house of the deceased at about 12 AM on 07.10.2020.
6. The father-in-law of the applicant opened the door and allowed all the assailants entry into the house.
Thereafter, the father-in-law went to his son's room, whereupon he was locked by the applicant and other co-accused persons in the said room.
7. According to the FIR, the deceased thereafter went on a spree of assaulting the two accused persons in a brutal manner.

The story set out in the FIR is highly improbable in as much as there was no cause for the father-in-law of the applicant to allow easy entry to the applicant and his five family members who were armed to teeth and were admittedly estranged with the first informant and his family.
8. There was no cause for the deceased to simply walk into his son's room instead of his own after the assailants had gained entry into the house.
9. The first informant claimed that he and his son watched the macabre incident through the window with grills.
The accused after committing the crime left his house.
Thereafter, both the witnesses namely the father-in-law and the brother-in-law of the applicant made good their escape through the ventilator in the same room.

10. The prosecution story becomes doubtful as the said witnesses had full opportunity to make good their escape or raise an alarm when the offence was being committed but they stood as mute spectators simply watching the incident.
11.
The other son of the first informant who was at the first floor was not alerted by the hue and cry raised by the victims at the time of the incident.
He was informed about the incident after the first informant freed himself.
However, the said witness in his statement before the investigating officer has stated that he was not present at the house at the time of the incident.
The first informant and his son have contradicted each other.

2 12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The police investigation also reveals that the almirahs of the household were broken into and the effects of the residents were rummaged through.
Clearly this was an armed dacoity which went wrong.
The applicant and his family members were convenient scapegoats.
13. All family members were implicated only to wreak vengeance upon the applicant.

14. It is noteworthy that one of the eye witness was having a mobile phone on his person at the time of the incident yet he did not alert his brother or informed the police when the incident was happening.
However, the Court does not propose to appraise the evidence at this stage as it may influence the trial.
15. There are other contradictions in the testimonies of the witnesses.
16. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated with the police investigations and had joined the trial.
17. The applicant never influenced witnesses or tampered with the evidence.
18. The trial is moving at a snail's pace and shows no signs of an early conclusion.
The applicant cannot be faulted for the delay in the trial.
19. The status report sent by the learned trial court records that the prosecution proposes to examine 25 witnesses to bring home the charges.
However, till date three witnesses including the eye witnesses have been examined.
There is no possibility of the applicant influencing the aforesaid witnesses.
20. The status report sent by the learned trial court also records that the prosecution witnesses did not attend the trial on appointed dates despite issuance of summons and other coercive measure.
21. The said witnesses are clearly trying to delay the trial only to prolong the incarceration of the applicant.
22. Inordinate delay in concluding trial has lead to an indefinite detention of the applicant without there being any credible evidence to implicate him in the offence.
Right of the applicant to a speedy trial has been violated.
23. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.

24. Continued incarceration of the applicant will disable him from framing an effective defence strategy, gathering evidence in his support thereof and tendering the same before the learned trial court to absolve himself.

Rishiraj Singh vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120237992/

sentences.text: The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.

entities.text: Prabhat Gangwar v. State of U.P. (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.2586 of 2023)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court has also to factor the likelihood of whether the accused committed the offence while deciding a bail application.

The court also has to determine in the facts of the case whether the accused needs to be set at liberty to frame his defence and gather evidence to refute the prosecution case and establish his innocence.
The bail court has to examine whether continued incarceration would disable the accused from tendering an effective defence of his case.
This is a demand of processual fairness in criminal jurisprudence.
Setting an accused at liberty at large on this ground cannot be applied mechanically in all cases.
The issue has to be considered in the facts and circumstances of each case while doing so.
All relevant facts including the evidences in the record, the conduct of the accused during the investigation as well as trial have to be adverted to before a decision is made in this regard."
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Rishiraj Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Order Date :- 16.2.2024 Vandit  Rishiraj Singh vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120237992/
